title: DLF Ltd - 532868 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: DLF posted a record FY26 collection of over INR 13,500 crore (+15% YoY) and zero gross debt in development, with FY26 sales bookings of INR 20,143 crore in line with guidance.
summary.overview: Management reported a strong close to FY26, citing record collections of over INR 13,500 crore (+15%) and cash surplus of over INR 7,700 crore (+25%). FY26 sales bookings were INR 20,143 crore, in line with guidance despite deferral of a couple of launches, with Q4 sales of about INR 3,967 crore led by Dahlias. Q4 consolidated revenue was about INR 2,452 crore with reported net profit of INR 1,256 crore; FY26 net profit was INR 4,256 crore (+16%). The rental business shows a 95% occupancy portfolio of 50 million sq ft and a 4-5 year NOI growth guidance of mid-teens, with 20-25% CAGR on a longer basis. Management steered the Q&A away from presales volume toward margins and cash flows.

financial_highlights.value: INR 14,155 crore, of which ~INR 11,200 crore in RERA escrow accounts

financial_highlights.metric: DCCDL FY26 revenue / EBITDA / PBT before exceptional
financial_highlights.value: ~INR 7,400 crore / over INR 5,700 crore / INR 2,726 crore

segments.name: Rental (annuity) business
segments.commentary: Rental portfolio of 50 million sq ft at 95% occupancy; FY26 NOI growth of about 34-35% driven by assets completed late FY25 reaching full lease. Non-SEZ office occupancy 98-99%, SEZ 88-89%, and income loss from vacancy down to ~3.5%.

segments.name: Development (DevCo)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales of INR 20,143 crore; Dahlias sales about INR 5,000 crore in FY26, guided to INR 5,000-6,000 crore in FY27. Management targets ~INR 9,000-10,000 crore of margin creation and INR 7,000-8,000 crore of DevCo FCF annually.

segments.name: Retail malls
segments.commentary: Existing mall income expected to grow 10-11% in FY27, plus three new malls. Midtown Plaza 95% leased and operational; Summit Plaza 95-97% leased, opening likely second half of July; Promenade Goa 50% leasing line of sight, completion around August.

segments.name: Office (Atrium Place, Downtown)
segments.commentary: Atrium Place (JV with Hines, 3.2 million sq ft) fully leased; three towers have OC and fourth tower OC expected Q2 FY27, generating ~INR 700 crore rent. Downtown Taramani 3.5 million sq ft ~500,000 sq ft leased, completion expected Q2 FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales guidance of ~INR 20,000 crore maintained; management said upside possible if demand stays strong.
Annual margin creation of ~INR 9,000 crore guided to continue.
Rental NOI guidance: mid-teens growth in NOI and 20-25% CAGR over the next 4-5 years, though management cautioned FY26's 34-35% growth should not be extrapolated.
FY27 exit rental of ~INR 8,200 crore across DCCDL and the rest of DLF assets combined.
Launch pipeline of almost INR 20,000 crore for FY27, including a large DLF City launch (INR 8,000-9,000 crore or higher), Arbour Senior Living, Westpark next phase, Dahlias, and possibly Goa.
Dividend: no formal guidance given; ~two-thirds of dividend is funded by Cyber City's dividend to DLF.
Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 (Towers 5-8) completion late FY28/early FY29; Taramani completion Q2 FY28.
capex_capacity: Atrium Place fourth tower OC expected Q2 FY27; Summit Plaza opening likely second half of July; Promenade Goa mall completion around August with opening 2-3 months later.
Downtown Taramani 3.5 million sq ft: completion expected Q2 FY28; central atrium design change made.

Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2: 7.5 million sq ft integrated development (2 million sq ft mall, 5.5 million sq ft offices); Tower 7 (2.2 million sq ft) nearly fully leased; Towers 5 and 6 being leased; finishing late FY28/early FY29; iconic tower construction to start in ~2.5 years.
Westpark Mumbai pipeline above 5 million sq ft; ~900,000 sq ft launched so far, next phase of ~800,000 sq ft in FY27, then 500,000-600,000 sq ft.
SEZ portfolio of 16-17 million sq ft; ~4 million sq ft converted to non-processing areas. Chennai operating portfolio above 10 million sq ft, rising to 14-15 million sq ft.
demand_pricing: Dahlias (super luxury, Gurugram): 32 apartments sold in Q4 plus 2 Camellias; per-unit prices now ~INR 90-110 crore for the first phase units vs ~INR 60-75 crore at launch. Dahlias per sq ft pricing is about INR 1 lakh on super area vs Camellias ~INR 1.2 lakh (INR 80-150 crore per unit).
Office SEZ rentals: gap to Cyber City rentals narrowed to 10-12% for new take-up; Cyber City vacancy lowest in SEZ portfolio; Hyderabad SEZ vacancy 17-20%.
Chennai Taramani top-floor leases at INR 145-150 per sq ft; average realisation expected INR 125-130 per sq ft.

Management flagged that large tenants are reviewing internal processes, which could defer leasing decisions, though no portfolio impact so far; cited AI and Iran-US war as factors but said there was no impact yet.
Management declined to chase presales volume, saying margins and cash flows are the priority; said presales of INR 50,000 crore a year are possible given land bank.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the medium-term launch pipeline shown as ~INR 60,000 crore versus INR 67,000 crore earlier, and is the company less confident about the market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure is a status update on a INR 1,14,000 crore 5-year launch pipeline announced ~2 years ago; launches are paced to market absorption and execution capacity, with further phases identified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 launch and presales plan given the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Aakash Ohri said the pipeline is ~INR 20,000 crore, including a DLF City launch of INR 8,000-9,000 crore or more, Arbour Senior Living, Westpark next phase, Dahlias, and possibly Goa (approvals in place but a PIL pending).

qa_highlights.question: Why is presales growth limited to ~INR 20,000 crore versus peers at INR 30,000-35,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Tyagi said presales is not the right metric and the company is chasing margins and cash flows; it could do INR 50,000 crore a year if chosen, with delivery capability the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the FY27 presales is expected from Dahlias and how much from the launch pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahlias sales were about INR 5,000 crore in FY26 and are expected at INR 5,000-6,000 crore in FY27; management expects INR 13,000-14,000 crore to come from the ~INR 20,000 crore launch pipeline, as not all launches will sell out at launch.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR 11,200 crore in RERA escrow accounts and the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Badal Bagri said the RERA cash unlocks from FY27-28; uses are shareholder returns, DLF rental capex (committed), and opportunistic margin-accretive land deals. Revenue recognition is on completed-contract method, with large projects like Arbour delivering from FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the dividend sustainable and how is it funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Tyagi said about two-thirds of the dividend comes from Cyber City's dividend to DLF, and no dividend guidance is being offered, though the trajectory has been of continuing growth.

risks_watch: Rental NOI growth of 34-35% in FY26 was driven by one-time lease-up of assets completed late FY25; management cautioned against extrapolation.
Large tenants reviewing decision-making (AI, Iran-US war), possibly deferring leasing; SEZ vacancy ~10% overall and 17-20% in Hyderabad.
Launch pipeline timing: Goa approvals subject to a PIL; Moti Nagar Phase 2 unlikely in FY27 and possibly FY28.
Dahlias sell-out and per-sq ft price trajectory is a key driver of FY27 presales; management admitted Dahlias pricing has moved fast.
Rising brokerage and overhead costs in Q4 linked to collections and year-end provisioning; management said full-year overheads should stay around current levels.
Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 and Taramani completion timelines, plus Atrium Place fourth tower OC expected Q2 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on cash flows, rental growth and Dahlias demand, but deliberately defensive on presales volume, which management said it is not chasing. Cautious on the tenant decision-making slowdown and on not extrapolating FY26 rental growth.
key_quotes: So, we are comfortable with generating this INR 9,000 to INR 10,000 crores of margin every year, generating about this INR 7,000 to INR8,000 crores of free cash flow every year on the Devco side.

I would request you not to take that as a basis for the future, because in our business, to construct the property and to bring it to market takes the cycle of 4 years, and every quarter and every year, it may not be the same.
Look Abhinav, dividend is driven by 2 pieces. A large chunk of this dividend is driven by Cyber City's dividend to us, frankly.
So, I mean, Gurgaon pricing of the super lux has, frankly, caught up, if not exceeded that in South Mumbai.

growth.why: FY27 sales guided at ~INR 20,000 crore (held, upside possible) and rental NOI mid-teens growth, backed by a ~INR 20,000 crore launch pipeline, leased mall/office completions (Summit Plaza, Promenade Goa, Atrium fourth tower) and 95% rental occupancy; no quarterly revenue or EBITDA growth figures were given in the brief.
